item.title: What Knowledge Was Worth: Office, Patronage, and Technical Power in Europe, c.1100–1850
item.description: A source-audited history of how European institutions converted different forms of knowledge into office, jurisdiction, property, patronage, clients, corporate recognition, and technical-state careers from c.1100 to c.1850. Rejects a simple law-to-mathematics succession in favor of multiple, overlapping prestige exchange rates.

item.title: The Calculus of the Wire: Oliver Heaviside and the Engineering of Electromagnetism
item.description: A source-audited history of Oliver Heaviside as a mathematical engineer who helped recast Maxwellian field theory, developed distributed transmission-line analysis and the distortionless-line condition, and built an operational calculus for solving circuit and field problems before its mathematical foundations were fully understood.
